title: Complete semantic i18n adoption across editor and supporting dialogs

needs: All remaining editor, preview, settings, export, and changelog product copy must use stable semantic catalog keys.
Dynamic warnings, errors, rendering states, export summaries, and provider states must use named placeholders.
Diagram source, prompts, generated diagrams, provider identity and credentials, file names, and changelog entry bodies must remain data.
The repository must enforce locale and placeholder parity and prevent new hardcoded product copy.
context: An initial convention slice established the repository i18n contract and migrated representative navigation copy.
The main editor still contains hardcoded labels, prompt guidance, placeholders, warnings, errors, and accessibility help.
Preview controls expose hardcoded rendering, zoom, and help states.
Settings, export, and changelog dialogs contain product headings, controls, statuses, confirmations, and accessibility attributes.

Provider names and descriptions may be configured or supplied externally; API keys and credentials are sensitive data; diagram source, prompts, generated output, and changelog entries are content rather than catalog copy.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Editor, preview, settings, export, and changelog surfaces render all product-owned visible and accessibility copy from stable semantic keys with locale parity.
AC2: Dynamic messages use named placeholders and locale-aware formatting with no sentence-shaped or rendered-value keys.
AC3: Diagram source, prompts, generated output, provider data, credentials, file names, and changelog entry content remain untranslated and are covered by boundary tests.
AC4: A static inventory and guard detect newly hardcoded product copy outside a narrow reviewed allowlist.
AC5: Contract validation, unit and UI tests, type checks, and production build pass for every supported locale.

product.title: Complete localized diagram editing experience
product.overview: Extend semantic localization to the complete editing workflow and its supporting dialogs while preserving authored, generated, configured, and sensitive values as data.
goals: Catalog every stable editor and dialog label, action, state, and accessibility description.
Use explicit placeholders for dynamic rendering, provider, and export feedback.
Keep authored and generated diagram content outside translation catalogs.
Make localization completeness part of routine repository validation.
non_goals: Translating diagram source, prompts, generated diagrams, file names, provider data, credentials, or changelog entry bodies.
Changing generation, rendering, export, storage, or provider behavior.
Adding new locales or a translation-management service.

backlog_items.title: Migrate editor, prompt, preview, and accessibility chrome
problem: The core editing workflow still embeds product labels, guidance, warnings, errors, rendering states, zoom controls, and assistive descriptions in components.
Those strings surround authored and generated diagram content that must never be translated.
scope_in: Migrate editor headings, prompt labels and guidance, placeholders, warnings, error framing, help text, preview states, zoom controls, actions, and accessibility attributes.
Use named placeholders for line or parse references, counts, zoom values, timing, and generation or rendering results.
Keep source text, prompts, generated diagram syntax, parser excerpts, and user-selected content as runtime data.
Add state-focused UI and accessibility tests for both locales.
scope_out: Translation or modification of diagram source, prompts, generated output, or parser-provided excerpts.
Changes to editing, generation, or rendering behavior.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Core editor and preview product chrome is fully catalog-driven.
AC2: Dynamic feedback uses named placeholders and locale-aware formatting.
AC3: Authored and generated content remains byte-for-byte identical across locale switches.
AC4: UI and accessibility tests cover idle, generating, rendering, warning, and error states.

backlog_items.title: Migrate settings and provider-control product copy
problem: Settings controls embed headings, instructions, statuses, credential actions, confirmations, and accessibility labels.
Provider metadata and credentials require a strict boundary from catalog-owned product copy.
scope_in: Migrate settings headings, field labels, guidance, provider-state framing, credential visibility and removal actions, confirmations, errors, and accessibility attributes.
Use named placeholders for provider references and status results while passing provider metadata as data.
Keep provider names and descriptions configurable and never catalog credentials, API keys, endpoints, or user-entered values.
Add tests for missing, configured, revealed, hidden, invalid, and removed credential states without exposing secret values.
scope_out: Changes to credential storage or provider integration.
Translation of provider brands, configured descriptions, endpoints, or secrets.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Settings product chrome uses semantic keys in every locale.
AC2: Provider statuses use named placeholders without turning provider metadata into keys.
AC3: No credential value is added to a catalog, log, fixture snapshot, or translation diagnostic.
AC4: Settings state tests pass in all supported locales.

backlog_items.title: Migrate export and changelog dialog chrome
problem: Export and changelog dialogs still contain product headings, format and scale labels, actions, help, loading, and empty states.
Export values and changelog entry bodies are content or data and must remain separate from stable dialog framing.
scope_in: Migrate export headings, format and scale controls, share guidance, actions, success and error framing, changelog headings, loading and empty states, and accessibility attributes.
Use named placeholders for formats, scales, dimensions, file names, versions, and export results.
Keep diagram output, file names, configured format identifiers, generated links, version numbers, and changelog entry bodies as data.
Add dialog tests for representative export and changelog states.
scope_out: Translation of exported diagram content or changelog entry bodies.
Changes to export or sharing behavior.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Export and changelog product chrome is fully catalog-driven.
AC2: Dynamic summaries use named placeholders.
AC3: Exported and versioned content remains unchanged across locales.
AC4: Dialog UI and accessibility tests pass in all locales.

backlog_items.title: Enforce catalog coverage and close the editor migration
problem: Conditional warnings, error branches, placeholders, titles, and accessibility attributes can escape manual review.
Without a guard, future editor changes can bypass semantic localization.
scope_in: Run a final inventory across source branches, attributes, notifications, dialogs, and helpers and classify every candidate.
Add a static guard with a narrow reviewed allowlist for tests, authored/generated content, provider data, technical literals, and credentials handling.
Validate semantic naming, catalog parity, placeholder parity, unused-key policy, and content-boundary fixtures.
Run contract validation and the complete repository test, type-check, and build matrix and record closure evidence.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The final inventory has no unclassified product-owned copy.
AC2: A failing fixture proves the guard rejects newly hardcoded product copy.
AC3: Catalog, placeholder, and content-boundary checks pass.
AC4: Full validation passes and closure evidence is recorded in Logics.

orchestration_task.title: Orchestrate completion of editor localization
plan: Baseline remaining strings and classify stable product copy versus authored, generated, configured, sensitive, and versioned data.
Migrate the core editor and preview first so the most frequent workflow establishes shared actions and status vocabulary.
Migrate settings with explicit credential-safety and provider-data tests.
Migrate export and changelog dialogs while preserving output and entry content.
Run the final inventory, enable the hardcoded-copy guard, and execute contract and repository validation.
Update all Logics documents and close the request only with catalog coverage, secret-safety, and content-boundary evidence.
